ai.literal: To do difficult what things are there than friendship? That like, for action difficult what things are there as defense?
ai.translation: What is as difficult to acquire as true friendship? And like it, what else can serve as such an impregnable defense for one's endeavors?
ai.modern: நட்பை விடச் சம்பாதிப்பதற்கு அரியவை வேறு எவை உள்ளன? அதுபோல, ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது அதற்குச் சிறந்த பாதுகாப்பாக அமையக்கூடியவை வேறு எவை உள்ளன?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of friendship by posing two rhetorical questions. First, it asks what is harder to acquire than a true friendship, implying that genuine friendship is the rarest and most precious achievement. Second, it asks what can offer a better shield or defense when undertaking any task. A true friend acts as a protective barrier, guiding and supporting one through difficult endeavors, making friendship both the hardest thing to attain and the greatest defense in life.

ai.literal: Having the nature of fullness is the friendship of those of noble character; having the nature of the moon's later stage is the friendship of fools.
ai.translation: The friendship of those of noble character is like the waxing moon that grows to fullness; the friendship of fools is like the waning moon that gradually fades away.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையோரின் நட்பு வளர்பிறை போல வளரும் தன்மை உடையது; அறிவிலிகளின் நட்பு தேய்பிறை போலத் தேயும் தன்மை உடையது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the nature of friendship to the phases of the moon. The friendship of wise and noble people (நீரவர்) is like the waxing moon (நிறைநீர), which starts small but steadily grows to complete fullness. In contrast, the friendship of foolish or ignorant people (பேதையார்) is like the waning moon (பிறைமதிப் பின்னீர), which may start large and bright but gradually diminishes until it disappears entirely. True friendship grows with time and understanding, while superficial friendship fades away.

ai.literal: Whenever studied, a book's delight is like, whenever associated with, the friendship of those possessing good character.
ai.translation: Just as a great book yields deeper delight every time it is read, so does the friendship of those with noble character grow sweeter the more one associates with them.
ai.modern: நூல்களைப் படிக்கப் படிக்க அவற்றின் நயம் மிகுவது போல, நற்பண்பு உடையவர்களோடு பழகப் பழக அவர்களுடைய நட்பு இன்பம் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the friendship of virtuous people to the reading of great books. A good book does not reveal all its beauty and wisdom on the first reading; instead, every time we re-read it, we discover new depths of meaning and delight. Similarly, the friendship of those with noble character does not grow stale; rather, the more we associate with them, the more we appreciate their goodness and find joy in their company. The poet beautifully uses the parallel of intellectual discovery to describe the emotional and moral growth found in true friendship.

ai.literal: Laughing for the purpose is not making friendship; when there is excess, going forward and reproving is the purpose.
ai.translation: Friendship is not made merely for the purpose of laughing and making merry; its true purpose is to go forward and sharply reprove a friend when they overstep bounds.
ai.modern: நட்புச் செய்தல் என்பது கூடிச் சிரித்து மகிழ்வதற்காக மட்டும் அன்று; நண்பர் தவறு செய்யும்போது அவரிடம் சென்று கடிந்து அறிவுரை கூறுவதற்காகவே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true purpose of friendship. It states that friendship is not meant merely for pleasant socializing, laughter, and amusement (நகுதல்). Instead, when a friend exceeds proper bounds or commits a wrong (மிகுதி), the true duty of a friend is to step forward (மேற்சென்று) and boldly reprove or correct them (இடித்தல்). The word 'இடித்தல்' literally means crushing or pounding, which metaphorically signifies sharp, uncompromising correction rather than gentle, ineffective advice. Thus, true friendship involves the courage to correct a friend for their own good.

ai.literal: Physical association and constant interaction are not necessary; shared feeling indeed will give the right of intimacy that is friendship.
ai.translation: Constant physical association and long familiarity are not necessary for friendship; a shared feeling alone will yield the right of intimate friendship.
ai.modern: நட்பு ஏற்படுவதற்கு உடலால் சேர்ந்து இருப்பதோ, பழகிக் கொண்டிருப்பதோ தேவையில்லை; மன உணர்வுகளின் ஒற்றுமை ஒன்றே நட்புக்குரிய உரிமையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that true friendship does not depend on physical proximity or long-term social interaction. The key words are 'புணர்ச்சி' (physical association) and 'பழகுதல்' (constant interaction), which are contrasted with 'உணர்ச்சி' (shared feeling or mental affinity). The poet asserts that 'உணர்ச்சி' alone is sufficient to create 'கிழமை', which means the right of intimacy or a deep bond of ownership between friends. Thus, true friendship is a union of minds rather than a mere habit of being together.

ai.literal: Smiling with the face, befriending is not friendship; of the heart, smiling with the heart, befriending is friendship.
ai.translation: A friendship that merely smiles with the face is not true friendship; true friendship is that which smiles from the depths of the heart.
ai.modern: முகம் மட்டும் மலரும்படி நட்புச் செய்வது உண்மையான நட்பு அன்று; உள்ளம் மகிழ்ந்து மலரும்படி நட்புச் செய்வதே உண்மையான நட்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet distinguishes between superficial friendship and genuine affection. The poet contrasts the outward appearance of the face with the inner reality of the heart. A smile that is only on the face when meeting someone does not constitute real friendship. True friendship is established only when the heart itself rejoices and smiles with sincere love.

ai.literal: Diverting from ruinous things, guiding in the right path, and sharing the suffering at the time of ruin is friendship.
ai.translation: True friendship is that which diverts one from ruinous paths, guides them along the path of virtue, and shares in their suffering when misfortune strikes.
ai.modern: தீய வழியிலிருந்து விலக்கி, நல்வழியில் செலுத்தி, துன்பம் வரும்போது உடன் இருந்து அந்தத் துன்பத்தைப் பகிர்ந்துகொள்வதே நட்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the active duties of a true friend. A real friend does not stand by idly; they actively steer one away from harmful paths and actions that lead to ruin. They then direct and guide one toward the path of virtue and goodness. Finally, if misfortune or ruin does strike, a true friend does not abandon them but stays to endure and share the grief and suffering.

ai.literal: Like the hand of one who lost his garment, immediately removing distress is friendship.
ai.translation: True friendship is that which instantly rushes to remove a friend's distress, just like the hand of a person whose garment slips off.
ai.modern: ஆடை நழுவியவனுடைய கை உடனே சென்று மானத்தைக் காப்பது போல, நண்பனுக்குத் துன்பம் வந்தபோது உடனே சென்று அத்துன்பத்தைப் போக்குவதே நட்பாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid and powerful analogy to define true friendship. When a person's garment slips, their hand acts instantly and instinctively to cover them, without any hesitation or conscious deliberation. Similarly, when a friend falls into distress, a true friend does not wait to be asked or hesitate, but immediately rushes to remove that suffering. The word 'āṅkē' (immediately) emphasizes the instantaneous nature of this help, and 'iṭukkaṇ kaḷaivatu' highlights that friendship is defined by active relief of distress.

ai.literal: If one asks what is the exalted seat of friendship, it is the state of supporting without wavering, in every possible way.
ai.translation: If one asks what is the sovereign throne of friendship, it is the unwavering stance of propping up a friend by all possible means whenever they falter.
ai.modern: நட்பின் சிறந்த இருப்பிடம் எது என்று கேட்டால், அது சற்றும் மனம் மாறாமல், இயன்ற போதெல்லாம் நண்பனைத் தாங்கிப் பிடிக்கும் நிலையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate height or 'sovereign seat' (vīṟṟirukkai) of true friendship. The poet explains that friendship is not merely about pleasant association, but about being an unwavering pillar of support. The word 'koṭpu' refers to wavering or changing one's mind; 'koṭpiṉṟi' means staying absolutely constant without turning away. 'Ollumvāy' refers to every possible opportunity or means available, and 'ūṉṟum nilai' is the active stance of propping up or supporting a friend when they are in distress.

ai.literal: Such persons these are to us, of such nature we are [to them], saying thus, even if praised, mean will be called friendship.
ai.translation: Even if one praises a friendship by boasting, 'They are of such great value to us, and we are of such nature to them,' that friendship becomes trivial and loses its dignity.
ai.modern: இவர் நமக்கு இப்படிப்பட்டவர், நாம் இவருக்கு இப்படிப்பட்டவர் என்று பெருமையாகச் சொன்னாலும், அந்த நட்பு தன் பெருமையை இழந்து சிறுமைப்பட்டுப் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet teaches that true friendship does not require boastful words or public declarations of mutual value. When friends start defining and measuring their relationship by saying, 'They are so good to us, and we are like this to them,' the friendship loses its natural depth and becomes trivial ('புல்'). True friendship is an unspoken, deep connection that does not need to be calculated or advertised. Embellishing or praising it with such words only diminishes its true worth.
